Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Jean Froissart (author, Wikidata Q315000), died 1410; Joseph Marie Bruno Constantin Kervyn de Lettenhove (editor, Wikidata Q725288), died 1891. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Froissart, Jean, 1338?-1410?; Kervyn de Lettenhove, Joseph Marie Bruno Constantin, Baron, 1817-1891 [Editor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's (Wikidata gives some of them several death years, every one 1925 or earlier: Jean Froissart [1405, 1410]).

Printed edition: Oeuvres de Froissart; publiées avec les variantes des divers manuscrits, Bruxelles, V. Devaux et cie, 1867, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/oeuvresdefroiss08belggoog. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 100%, 85%, 46% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Joseph Marie Bruno Constantin Kervyn de Lettenhove, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
